description: Machine-parseable registry of all known bugs with root cause analysis, regression test links, and pattern categorization.

root_cause_categories.path_error: Wrong file path or directory reference
root_cause_categories.schema_drift: Expected vs actual data shape mismatch
root_cause_categories.silent_failure: Error swallowed without logging or effect
root_cause_categories.mapping_error: Wrong value translation or type coercion
root_cause_categories.dead_code: Code that writes to a file or endpoint nothing reads
root_cause_categories.platform_compat: Code assumes one OS or runtime (POSIX-only modules, default text encodings, path separators, shell availability)

bugs.title: outcome_engine reads from wrong evidence path
bugs.description: outcome_engine.py read outcomes from .soma/outcomes.jsonl instead of the canonical .soma/evidence/outcomes.jsonl path.
bugs.pattern: Hardcoded paths diverge from actual evidence directory structure

bugs.title: outcome_engine expects wrong schema key
bugs.description: outcome_engine.py expected cells_used (list) but MCP tools wrote cell_id (string). Both schemas were valid in different writers.
bugs.pattern: Multiple writers produce different schemas for the same data, reader expects only one

bugs.title: sync.py silently ignores agent outcomes
bugs.description: sync.py did not map success/failure outcome strings to tp/fp counters. Agent-reported outcomes were silently dropped.
bugs.pattern: Outcome value vocabulary not shared between writer and reader

bugs.title: sync.py clobbers scores on missing outcome data
bugs.description: When a cell had triggers but zero tp/fp records, sync.py set score = 0.0 instead of preserving the existing score. Un-evaluated cells were treated as 100% failures.
bugs.pattern: Absence of evidence treated as evidence of absence

bugs.title: Dead-end .soma/cells/fitness.jsonl file
bugs.description: outcome_engine.py and cell_selection.sh wrote to .soma/cells/fitness.jsonl but nothing read it. The canonical evidence ledger was at .soma/evidence/fitness.jsonl.
bugs.pattern: Writer and reader disagree on canonical file location

bugs.title: diagnose_hot_zones.py uses Python 3.10+ type syntax
bugs.description: diagnose_hot_zones.py used dict | None union type syntax (PEP 604) which requires Python 3.10+. CI matrix includes Python 3.9, causing TypeError during test collection.
bugs.pattern: Type annotation syntax incompatible with minimum supported Python version

bugs.title: pyproject.toml version desynchronized from VERSION file
bugs.description: VERSION file was bumped but pyproject.toml was missed during the release procedure, causing CI pipeline failure on test_version_is_single_sourced.
bugs.pattern: Duplicated configuration values fall out of sync during manual procedures

bugs.title: MCP server crashes on Windows: unconditional `import fcntl`
bugs.description: soma_mcp/tools.py (since v0.60) and soma_sdk/telemetry.py import fcntl unconditionally, so `python -m soma_mcp` exits with ModuleNotFoundError on Windows and MCP hosts get no Soma tools. v0.52 fixed this only in enzymes/fitness_updater.py. Fixed by guarding both imports with try/except ImportError and skipping flock when fcntl is None, matching fitness_updater.py. Appends are unlocked on Windows.
bugs.pattern: Fix applied to one call site of a shared pattern, not to all of them

bugs.title: MCP write/execute tools unusable from MCP hosts: `_sessionToken` is only returned in serverInfo
bugs.description: Since v0.86 the server returns a per-process random token only as serverInfo._sessionToken and requires it as a tool argument for the 3 write tools and 6 execute tools. MCP hosts handle `initialize` themselves and don't pass serverInfo to the model, and the tool schemas don't declare the argument. So only the 5 read tools are usable, outcomes can't be reported, and fitness never evolves. Not platform-specific.
bugs.pattern: Auth handshake designed for a direct client, not for the host-mediated MCP protocol

bugs.title: Windows: installer tests wrote to the real user profile
bugs.description: Running pytest on Windows rewrote ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, created ~/.kiro (128 files), and overwrote ~/.soma/manifest.json and ~/.soma/backup in the real profile. Cause, confirmed: under Git Bash enzymes/common.sh resolve_home() prefers USERPROFILE over HOME, and six install/uninstall calls in tests/test_install_lifecycle.py overrode only HOME, so install.sh and uninstall.sh ran against the real Windows profile. The shared tests/conftest.py run() helper now sets USERPROFILE to HOME whenever a caller overrides HOME alone. Verified on Windows 11 with HOME and USERPROFILE pointed at a scratch directory around the whole suite: before the fix the lifecycle tests wrote .claude/CLAUDE.md, .soma/manifest.json and backups into it; after, it stays empty and the real profile is unchanged. Five lifecycle tests still fail on Windows because of BUG-036 (#62). The Git Bash python3 stub, previously tracked here, is now BUG-037.
bugs.pattern: Test isolation relies on HOME overrides that the code under test does not honor

bugs.title: Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot parse the PowerShell installers (no UTF-8 BOM)
bugs.description: install.ps1, install/install.ps1 and install/uninstall.ps1 are UTF-8 without a BOM. Windows PowerShell 5.1, which `.\install.ps1` runs on stock Windows, decodes them as cp1252. The em-dash's trailing 0x94 byte becomes a closing quote, so parsing fails and nothing is installed. CI misses this because validate.yml runs pwsh 7, which defaults to UTF-8. Fixed by saving the three .ps1 files as UTF-8 with BOM. A static test now requires a BOM on every non-ASCII .ps1, and the Windows CI job dry-runs the installer under Windows PowerShell 5.1.
bugs.pattern: CI tests a different runtime (pwsh 7) than the one users run (Windows PowerShell 5.1)

bugs.title: Implicit cp1252 encoding on Windows: `soma status` crash, list_cells garbled or dropped cells
bugs.description: With stdout on cp1252 (Windows, redirected output), `soma status` printed an emoji, raised UnicodeEncodeError and exited 1; enzymes/verify_bug_registry.py crashed the same way when printing its error report. Both entry points now reconfigure stdout with errors='replace', so unencodable characters print as '?'. The list_cells half (bare read_text() inside `except Exception: pass`, which garbled non-ASCII text and dropped undecodable cells) was fixed in the v0.89.0 pre-release review by the explicit UTF-8 canonical inventory; verified on Windows with a cp1252 locale and a cell containing curly quotes, an em-dash, an emoji and 'Ð' (byte 0x90). tests/test_rule_metadata.py read rule files with bare read_text() and failed 6 cases on genome/subagent-delegation.md; it now reads UTF-8 explicitly.
bugs.pattern: Relying on the platform default encoding instead of an explicit utf-8

bugs.title: Windows-only test failures: unescaped paths, separators, CRLF, bash and symlink assumptions
bugs.description: Test-only Windows failures, all fixed in the tests: (1) test_branch_coverage.py and test_mutation_tester.py wrote `sys.path.insert(0, '{tmp_path}')` into generated test files; a Windows path contains `\U`, so the file failed with a unicodeescape SyntaxError. They now use `{str(tmp_path)!r}`. (2) test_init.py compared str(WindowsPath) against POSIX separators; it now compares Path.parts. test_packaging_install_correctness.py compared the C:/... paths written under Git Bash against backslash paths; it now normalizes both. (3) test_enforce_hooks.py wrote the bash hook in text mode (CRLF, locale encoding) and test_outcome_engine_insights.py wrote JSONL with CRLF while asserting a byte offset; both now write UTF-8 with LF. (4) The conftest `bash` fixture returned None when bash was missing, and test_uninstall_confinement.py and test_v089_review_followups.py hard-coded /bin/bash (WinError 2); a conftest require_bash() helper now resolves bash or skips. (5) Symlink tests skip when symlinks need a privilege (WinError 1314), and the POSIX execute-bit test skips on Windows. Verified on Windows 11 / Python 3.14: the full suite went from 49 to 12 failures, all BUG-036 or BUG-038. Note: with coverage missing from the environment, branch_coverage fails closed (lines [-1]); coverage is a declared dev dependency.
bugs.pattern: Tests assert on OS-specific string forms

bugs.title: PowerShell installer writes mojibake into generated rule files
bugs.description: With the parse failure worked around, install/install.ps1 reads rule files with Get-Content and no -Encoding. PS 5.1 decodes UTF-8 as cp1252, putting garbled sequences into generated files. Fixed by enforcing explicit UTF8 on all rule/config reads, preserving the PowerShell BOM, and integrating native Python lifecycle hook execution in v0.93.0.
bugs.pattern: Relying on the platform default encoding instead of an explicit utf-8

bugs.title: `soma checkpoint` / `soma sync` wipe cell fitness on a fresh clone (triggers→0, score→null)
bugs.description: The evidence .gitignore excludes fitness.jsonl (trigger events) while outcomes.jsonl (170 tp/fp records) is committed. On a fresh clone, aggregate_evidence returns triggers=0 with tp>0 for each cell that has outcomes. sync_frontmatter then overwrites `triggers` with 0 and sets score = tp/t, which is None when t == 0. Running `soma checkpoint`, which the pre-commit hook runs, reset all 41 such cells in a clean worktree of develop. A check command thereby rewrites tracked cell files, and a pre-commit run can commit the wiped fitness. Fixed in the pre-release review by making checkpoint byte-for-byte read-only and rebuilding sync on the canonical signals ledger with independent dimension presence, atomic replacement, and fail-closed parse handling.
bugs.pattern: Derived state recomputed from a partially-versioned evidence set overwrites the recorded state

bugs.title: MCP canonical-workspace injection was unreachable; tools honoured a client-supplied workspace
bugs.description: In soma_mcp/server.py the `args["workspace"] = _canonical_workspace` assignment sat after the unconditional return of the soma_request_receipt branch, so it never ran. Handlers used `args.get('workspace')`, so a caller could request and redeem a receipt naming another Soma workspace and mutate it; read tools also accepted a client workspace. Fixed by stripping server-owned keys from every tool call and injecting the operator-configured workspace after receipt verification; privileged calls fail closed if no canonical workspace is configured.
bugs.pattern: Security control placed after an unconditional return

bugs.title: MCP receipts were bound to empty file and cell digests
bugs.description: issue_receipt and verify_receipt were called with file_digest="" and cell_digest="", so editing the target file or the governance cells between issuance and redemption did not invalidate a receipt. Fixed by computing sha256 digests of the target paths named in the arguments and of every cell under .soma/cells at issuance, recomputing them at redemption, and rejecting paths that escape the workspace.
bugs.pattern: Integrity field populated with a constant placeholder

bugs.title: Telemetry event_id was computed but never enforced
bugs.description: append_signal hashed an event_id but appended unconditionally, so retries duplicated evidence and a changed payload reused the id silently. Fixed: identity excludes signal type and metadata, a payload_digest is stored, and under a cross-process evidence lock an identical replay is a no-op while a different payload raises EventConflictError.
bugs.pattern: Idempotency key written but never read

bugs.title: Epoch migration did not convert, reconcile or fence evidence writers
bugs.description: run_epoch_migration copied fitness.jsonl and rewrote epoch_generation with a plain write. It did not convert legacy outcomes/fitness rows into signals.jsonl, reconcile counts, write atomically, or reject writers from the previous generation, and the telemetry lock check was check-then-act. Fixed: the cutover holds the evidence lock, snapshots every ledger with SHA256SUMS, converts rows with deterministic event ids (skipping MCP twins and already-migrated rows), aborts unchanged on a reconciliation mismatch, replaces files atomically, and stamps a generation that append_signal(expected_generation=...) enforces.
bugs.pattern: Lock-and-counter placeholder presented as a fenced migration

bugs.title: Human-insight cursor advanced before the insights were persisted
bugs.description: capture_human_insight_signals wrote the byte-offset cursor before main() updated cell fitness or appended signals, so a crash or failed append permanently skipped those insights, and a partial trailing line could be skipped. Fixed by splitting read (no write, complete lines only) from an atomic commit that main() performs only after a successful update and append.
bugs.pattern: Progress marker committed before the work it records

bugs.title: Uninstall manifest paths were confined by a lexical prefix check only
bugs.description: uninstall.sh accepted `$HOME/safe/../../outside/victim` and paths under a symlinked directory, skipped unsafe entries silently, never checked backup_dir, and did not re-check at the rm/sed sink. uninstall.ps1 only normalised separators. Fixed: both uninstallers validate every manifest field and the full removal plan against canonical allowed roots (no ./.. segments, no symlinked or reparse-point ancestors) before any mutation, fail closed, and re-check each path immediately before removal.
bugs.pattern: String prefix check used as path containment

bugs.title: quality_gate crashes on Python 3.14: ast.Str was removed
bugs.description: immune_system/verification/quality_gate.py referenced ast.Str, removed in Python 3.14, so check_no_bare_pass raised AttributeError on stub test bodies. ast.Constant already covers string literals since Python 3.8.
bugs.pattern: Deprecated stdlib alias removed in a newer runtime

bugs.title: Release tested checkout code and published untested, unverified artifacts
bugs.description: validate.yml installed `ls dist/*.whl | head -n 1` but ran tests from the checkout, where pythonpath=['.'] shadows the wheel; publish.yml uploaded dist/* (including the never-tested sdist) without a digest check. Fixed: one build records SHA256SUMS; the sdist and the matrix-installed wheel are smoke-tested from outside the checkout in isolated mode with module origins asserted under site-packages; publish verifies digests and uploads only the verified files.
bugs.pattern: Tested artifact and shipped artifact not provably identical

bugs.title: Canonical evidence batches were not atomic or retry-safe
bugs.description: Multi-cell producers appended one signal at a time; a failure after the first row left a partial batch, and MCP report_outcome dual-wrote a legacy outcomes row before signals. Fixed with append_signals: validate/dedupe the complete batch under one cross-process lock and atomically replace the ledger; report_outcome requires an idempotency key and writes only canonical signals.
bugs.pattern: Per-item appends used for an operation that must commit as one batch

bugs.title: Migration lease could be stolen from a live owner or delete a successor lock
bugs.description: An old mtime marked a lock stale even when os.kill proved its PID alive, and unconditional cleanup could unlink a replacement lock. The lock now carries an unpredictable owner token, live PIDs are never age-stolen, dead owners are reclaimable, and release unlinks only its own token.
bugs.pattern: Lease age treated as stronger evidence than live ownership

bugs.title: Active readers continued consuming retired evidence ledgers
bugs.description: Status, report, oracle, lifecycle, checkpoint and session-close readers disagreed on fitness.jsonl, outcomes.jsonl and signals.jsonl. A stdlib soma_core.evidence aggregator now provides canonical weighted signals, independent trigger/outcome dimensions, and structured parse errors; active readers use it while legacy files remain migration inputs only.
bugs.pattern: Writer migration completed without migrating all readers

bugs.title: Cell cache and receipt digest observed different or stale cell trees
bugs.description: The cache used a maximum float mtime and followed recursive glob symlinks while receipt hashing did not. Restored mtimes could serve stale governance, stat errors could return an empty inventory, and symlink directories escaped the digest boundary. The canonical cell inventory captures exact bytes, content fingerprints, and race metadata without following links; cache, receipts, MCP and SDK listing share it and fail closed.
bugs.pattern: Security-sensitive consumers used different filesystem inventories

bugs.title: Checkpoint skipped unreadable and malformed inputs
bugs.description: Checkpoint treated source read/stat failures and malformed cell/evidence input as absence, allowing a pass on incomplete evidence. Checks now return path-bearing issues, reject symlink/non-regular inputs, consume canonical evidence, and remain recursively read-only on pass and fail.
bugs.pattern: Verification converted read/parse failure into a clean result

bugs.title: Generated MCP configs governed the checkout and clobbered other servers
bugs.description: Bash/PowerShell installers and soma init used SOMA_ROOT/source cwd or overwrote the whole MCP JSON. Generators now merge mcpServers.soma atomically, preserve unrelated keys/servers, bind cwd and SOMA_WORKSPACE to the governed project, and add a source PYTHONPATH fallback only when the package is not installed.
bugs.pattern: Installer configuration targeted its own source instead of the governed project

bugs.title: Distribution leaked project evidence and omitted the full genome
bugs.description: The sdist recursively included .soma evidence/dreams/locks while the wheel omitted top-level genome rules, so source-hidden soma init --rules full failed. Packaging now prunes .soma, packages genome markdown as resources, synchronizes Python/JS versions, and the wheel/sdist smoke installs all full rules outside the checkout.
bugs.pattern: Source-tree tests concealed missing wheel data and private sdist data

bugs.title: Install ownership and manifestless cleanup could delete unrelated user configuration
bugs.description: PowerShell wrote no exact manifest and Bash manifestless fallback enrolled all Markdown/skills. Both installers now record exact ownership including MCP configs; uninstall removes only mcpServers.soma or source-owned names, preflights config JSON, and validates restore paths at the copy sink.
bugs.pattern: Fallback discovery treated shared directories as exclusively owned

bugs.title: Native PowerShell installer does not install lifecycle hooks
bugs.description: install.ps1 now deploys native hooks via Install-Hooks and `soma hook` / `python -m soma_cli.hooks <phase>`, eliminating the bash dependency on Windows. Installed hooks are recorded in manifest.json and cleaned on uninstall.ps1.
bugs.pattern: Cross-platform support claimed while one platform omits a lifecycle subsystem

bugs.title: `soma status` reports the wrong core-rule count for installer-based Claude setups
bugs.description: install.sh/install.ps1 merge all rules into ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, but soma_cli/status.py globs the rules directory for *.md excluding CLAUDE.md, and with no loose files it falls back to the package's own genome/. Reproduced on v0.89.0 with an isolated HOME: a 1-rule CLAUDE.md reports '19 active' (the genome/ count); the same CLAUDE.md plus 2 loose .md files reports '2 active'. Fixed: status now parses the Soma sections of CLAUDE.md in both formats that write it (the installers' '# Soma Governance Rules' header with '---' + H1 per rule, and soma init's SOMA:START/END block with '## <stem>' sections), adds loose rule files, drops merged sections that duplicate a loose file by stem, frontmatter id or H1, and no longer falls back to genome/ when CLAUDE.md holds Soma content. Merged installer sections are named by mapping their H1 back to the packaged rule id, so trigger counts still match.
bugs.pattern: Status reads a different artifact than the installer writes

bugs.title: mutation_tester fails open: unrunnable tests count as killing every mutant
bugs.description: check() never runs the tests against the unmutated source first, and _run_tests() treats any non-zero pytest exit (collection error, import error, timeout, exception) as a killed mutant. Reproduced on v0.89.0: for `add(a, b)` with a test file containing a syntax error, check() returns verdict=True, '0/2 survived'. The verdict feeds the arbiter's TAUTOLOGICAL_TEST signal, so broken tests are rated as strong. It also masks BUG-013 on Windows. Fixed: check() now runs the tests against the unmutated source first; if they fail it returns verdict=False, lines=[-1] and a 'Baseline tests fail' detail, matching branch_coverage's fail-closed convention. A mutant that times out or errors after a passing baseline still counts as killed.
bugs.pattern: Verifier treats 'could not run' as 'passed' (fail-open)

bugs.title: Windows: cell inventory rejected edited cells, breaking soma_scan, list_cells and every receipt
bugs.description: _read_stable_file() compared an os.stat(path) signature against os.fstat(fd), and the signature included st_ctime_ns. On Windows os.stat reports st_ctime as the creation time and os.fstat as the last-change time, so any cell written after creation raised CellInventoryError 'file changed before it was opened'. soma_scan and soma_list_cells failed and soma_request_receipt returned 'Internal error', so no write or execute MCP tool could run on Windows. The same function opened cells without O_BINARY, so Windows text mode turned CRLF into LF and the snapshot bytes differed from disk. st_ctime_ns is now left out of the signature on Windows (st_ino, st_size and st_mtime_ns still detect changes), and cells are opened with O_BINARY.
bugs.pattern: Stat signatures compared across os.stat and os.fstat assume both report the same timestamps

bugs.title: uninstall.sh under Git Bash rejects every path as 'not an absolute path'
bugs.description: Under Git Bash, resolve_home returns `cygpath -u "$USERPROFILE"`, so RESOLVED_HOME, the allowed roots and every removal-plan entry are MSYS paths (/c/Users/..., /tmp/...). uninstall.sh's embedded Python check() runs in native Windows Python, where os.path.isabs() rejects them, so uninstall refuses every entry and removes nothing (fails closed). Git for Windows ships no Python, so python3 there is normally a native build. On Windows this fails the BUG-031 regression tests and five tests in tests/test_install_lifecycle.py. (Corrected when fixed: an earlier version of this entry said the refusal tests in tests/test_uninstall_confinement.py passed on Windows only because every entry was refused. Hostile native-form manifests were in fact already refused with their specific reasons at manifest validation; it was the later removal-plan check, fed MSYS paths on stdin, that refused everything.) Fixed in uninstall.sh's confinement check: MSYS-form paths are mapped with cygpath after the ./.. segment check (cygpath folds ..); the shell resolves cygpath from PATH and passes its absolute path, because a bare name in native Windows Python also searches the current directory (the project being uninstalled). Fixing it exposed three more defects, also fixed: read_manifest_field wrote CRLF in the console code page, so every entry but the last and non-ASCII names silently dropped out of the plan; an entry it could not encode (a lone surrogate) ended the list early, after which uninstall exited 0 and deleted the manifest; and a refusal could crash while printing its own path. Hardening found while investigating: on Windows the check now refuses segments ending in a space or dot and ':' stream syntax, which Win32 resolves to a different name than the one checked. A sandbox probe of 15 such shapes found none that made uninstall.sh (or uninstall.ps1 under Windows PowerShell 5.1) delete anything outside the roots, because rm takes the name literally; PowerShell 7 was not tested.
bugs.pattern: POSIX-form paths handed to a native Windows interpreter

bugs.title: Git Bash: python3 can resolve to the Windows Store stub, so hooks and shell-script Python calls fail
bugs.description: A python.org install provides python.exe but no python3.exe, so in Git Bash `python3` resolves to the App Installer stub. `command -v python3` succeeds, but running it exits 49 with no output. enzymes/common.sh install_hooks() therefore renders an empty hooks.json and skips hooks, and the other python3 calls in install/ and enzymes/*.sh fail the same way. Workaround: disable the python3 App execution alias and put a real python3 on PATH. Split out of BUG-010 when its home-isolation half was fixed. Suggested fix: resolve one working interpreter (python3, python, py -3), accepting a candidate only if it runs `-c 'import sys'`, and use it everywhere.
bugs.pattern: Interpreter presence checked with command -v instead of by running it

bugs.title: Windows: enzyme scripts crash on a cp1252 stdout when printing non-ASCII
bugs.description: Nineteen standalone enzyme scripts and immune_system/verification/runner.py print emoji, arrows or other non-ASCII characters from their __main__ entry points without reconfiguring stdout. With stdout on cp1252 (Windows, redirected or captured, including hook runs under Git Bash) they raise UnicodeEncodeError and exit 1. Seen on Windows in tests/test_crossover_structured.py: enzymes/cell_crossover.py fails at its 'Crossover: a x b -> c' line (U+2192). Same class as BUG-012, which fixed the `soma` CLI and verify_bug_registry.py only. (Corrected when fixed: a wider scan found nine more __main__ scripts with non-ASCII output literals; three of them (cell_fitness, cell_adversarial, immune_entropy) were confirmed to crash with no arguments; cell_fitness is run by Governance.fitness_landscape and session_close.sh.) Fixed: all 29 entry points reconfigure stdout with errors='replace' as the first statement of their __main__ block, the same guard as BUG-012, so modules imported by soma_cli and soma_mcp leave the caller's stdout alone. tests/test_enzyme_console_encoding.py runs 12 of them under PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 against a UTF-8 run, and a structural test requires the guard in every __main__ script with a non-ASCII string literal outside a docstring.
bugs.pattern: Relying on the platform default encoding instead of an explicit utf-8

bugs.title: mutation_tester counted comparison, boolean, statement and return mutations but never applied them
bugs.description: _apply_mutation_by_index() first built a target list holding only binary-operator, unary-operator and constant mutations and returned None when the index was past it. _collect_mutations() also collects comparison, and/or, statement-deletion and return-value mutations, so those were counted in the total but skipped by check(): neither killed nor survived. A test that never checks a comparison passed: `def eq(a, b): return a == b` with a test that calls eq(1, 2) without asserting got verdict=True, '0/2 survived'. The incomplete first pass is removed; the complete, order-matched target list now decides every mutation. Applying every kind exposed two equivalent mutants that no test can kill (deleting a docstring, and `return None` -> `return None`); both are no longer generated. Found by the independent review of BUG-034.
bugs.pattern: Collected mutations silently skipped instead of being evaluated

bugs.title: Recording an outcome leaves .soma/evidence/.signals.lock as an untracked file
bugs.description: soma_sdk.telemetry.evidence_lock() creates .soma/evidence/.signals.lock (open with 'a+b') the first time any signal is appended, including a soma_report_outcome call that records nothing (cells_used=[]). Neither the root .gitignore nor .soma/evidence/.gitignore covers it, so after one MCP outcome report the repository has an untracked .soma/evidence/.signals.lock, which `git add -A` would commit. Seen live on 2026-10-02 during the BUG-009/BUG-035 receipt check through the MCP server; not Windows-specific. Related: .soma/evidence/.fitness.lock is a committed, empty file that no current code creates or reads. Fixed by adding .signals.lock to .soma/evidence/.gitignore; the lock file itself is kept, since deleting it after use could race with another process taking the lock. This covers the Soma repository only: soma init writes no .soma/evidence/.gitignore into other workspaces, and that is unchanged.
bugs.pattern: Runtime lock file written inside the working tree without an ignore rule

bugs.title: soma CLI not found under zsh after pip install --user, with no guidance
bugs.description: pip install --user puts the soma console script in the user scripts directory (~/.local/bin on Linux). Debian/Ubuntu add it to PATH only in ~/.profile, which zsh does not read, so on a stock oh-my-zsh setup `soma` is 'command not found'. Seen on 2026-10-03. Nothing said why: the Makefile discarded pip's stderr (hiding pip's own not-on-PATH warning) and its PATH check was a substring grep for $HOME/.local/bin, wrong for venvs, macOS and Windows; soma doctor reported the failure without a remedy; `python3 -m soma_cli` did not work; and the docs never mentioned PATH. Fixed with soma_cli/pathcheck.py, which finds the directory pip used (sysconfig scripts paths), checks exact PATH entries, detects zsh/bash/fish/PowerShell and prints the one line to add and the rc file it belongs in. It never edits dotfiles. soma doctor, the end of install.sh and install.ps1 print it; the Makefile now uses python3 -m pip and shows pip's errors only when every install attempt fails. Also added soma_cli/__main__.py and soma --version, and a troubleshooting section in QUICKSTART.md. MCP was not affected: its config launches python3 -m soma_mcp.
bugs.pattern: Installer assumes the user's shell reads the same startup file as bash

bugs.title: immune_sweep.sh aborts with 'RESOLVED_HOME: unbound variable' unless SOMA_DATA_DIR is exported
bugs.description: enzymes/immune_sweep.sh defaults SOMA_DATA_DIR to $RESOLVED_HOME/.gemini/antigravity, but nothing in the script set RESOLVED_HOME. It runs under set -euo pipefail, so with SOMA_DATA_DIR unset the sweep exited 1 at line 28 before doing any work. Fixed: RESOLVED_HOME is set from common.sh's resolve_home.
bugs.pattern: Variable read under set -u that no code path assigns

bugs.title: uninstall.sh without a working Python 3 fell back to a symlink-blind lexical confinement check
bugs.description: install/uninstall.sh check_confined() used _lexical_confined whenever no working Python 3 was found. Fixed: without a working interpreter check_confined() refuses every target, and non-empty plan is refused before anything is touched.
bugs.pattern: Security check degrades to a weaker fallback instead of failing closed

bugs.title: Inline Python in enzymes, install.sh and uninstall.sh imported modules from the current directory
bugs.description: python -c CODE and python - <<heredoc put current directory at sys.path[0]. Fixed: soma_py strips CWD entry from sys.path[0] for inline code while preserving user site-packages.
bugs.pattern: Inline interpreter code run with the current directory on the import path

bugs.title: uninstall.sh rewrote Claude settings.json outside the confinement guard, plan preview and --dry-run
bugs.description: The settings.json cleanup at the end of uninstall.sh ran jq del(.hooks.soma) without guard_sink/check_confined or plan preview. Fixed: settings files carrying hooks.soma are queued during planning, previewed as [MOD], and confined.
bugs.pattern: File rewrite that bypasses the path confinement guard

bugs.title: enzymes/verify_bug_registry.py timed out on clean Windows installation (#80)
bugs.description: Fixed 30s budget for running all bug regression tests was exceeded on Windows. Fixed by dynamic budget math based on number of regression test cases and node matching by pytest summary IDs.
bugs.pattern: Fixed timeout budget for growing test suite

bugs.title: soma init pre-commit hook aborted every commit with 'soma: not found' when soma was not on the hook's PATH
bugs.description: The marked block install_hook() writes into .git/hooks/pre-commit ran a bare `soma checkpoint --pre-commit`. Git runs hooks with the PATH of the process that started it, so in zsh or other non-login shells after `pip install --user` (BUG-041), GUI git clients and IDEs, `soma` did not resolve and git aborted the commit with only `soma: not found`. Re-running `soma init` could not repair it, because install_hook() returned early once the marker was present. Fixed: the block (POSIX sh) runs `soma` when it is on PATH, otherwise the interpreter that ran `soma init` (sys.executable, shell-quoted) with `-m soma_cli checkpoint --pre-commit` after checking it can import soma_cli; with neither it prints a message naming `soma doctor` and the PATH fix and exits 1 (still fail-closed). A checkpoint failure now exits the hook explicitly instead of depending on the block being last. Re-running `soma init` replaces an existing marked block in place, keeping user lines outside the markers, and `soma doctor` reports a block without the `soma-hook-format: 2` marker as stale.
bugs.pattern: Hook or generated script that depends on the interactive shell's PATH

bugs.title: enzymes/ttc_verifier.py fails to resolve escalation_sentinel.sh in external consumer projects
bugs.description: ttc_verifier.py resolved escalation_sentinel.sh via os.path.join(workspace, 'enzymes', ...). External projects lack an enzymes/ folder, forcing false ESCALATION_REQUIRED on all proposals.
bugs.pattern: Assuming workspace contains engine installation directory structure

bugs.title: enzymes/cell_create_nl.py cell_type parameter path traversal vulnerability
bugs.description: cell_create_nl.py joined unvalidated cell_type string into filename f'{cell_type}-{slug}.md', permitting directory traversal outside of .soma/cells/.
bugs.pattern: Joining unvalidated parameter into filesystem path without basename sanitization

bugs.title: enzymes/bump_version.sh version string unvalidated regex substitution code injection
bugs.description: bump_version.sh substituted unvalidated version argument $1 directly into Python code in soma_sdk/__init__.py, allowing arbitrary code execution upon import.
bugs.pattern: Unvalidated shell parameter substituted into executable code template

bugs.title: soma_mcp/tools.py soma_propose_change drops workspace parameter
bugs.description: soma_mcp/tools.py omitted workspace argument when calling soma_propose_change, causing path confinement to evaluate against os.getcwd() instead of _canonical_workspace.
bugs.pattern: Omitting workspace parameter in MCP tool execution router

bugs.title: Core enzymes swallow cell parse errors with bare except Exception: pass
bugs.description: cell_scan.py, cell_deps.py, cell_coverage.py, and immune_grade.py swallowed cell parsing exceptions silently, un-guarding security paths.
bugs.pattern: Bare except pass swallowing exception without stderr output or logging

bugs.title: soma_mcp/tools.py soma_verify_changes falsely attests layer1_only: false without executing Layer 2
bugs.description: soma_verify_changes returned layer1_only: false status PASS without running Layer 2 adversarial verification.
bugs.pattern: Returning pass response with unverified capability claims

bugs.title: soma_sdk/cells.py top-level import yaml breaches zero-deps MCP wall
bugs.description: soma_sdk/cells.py contained top-level import yaml, causing allowlisted insight_capture enzyme to crash on bare Python interpreters.
bugs.pattern: Transitive import of non-stdlib dependency in stdio server path

bugs.title: enzymes/session_close.sh git sync order inversion leaves cell evolution uncommitted
bugs.description: session_close.sh executed git commit && git push before outcome_engine.py and cell_fitness.py ran, leaving cell evolution updates dirty on exit.
bugs.pattern: Git push executed before lifecycle mutation steps complete

bugs.title: soma_mcp/cell_cache.py fails open on HMAC signature failure
bugs.description: CellCache._verify_integrity emitted warning on STDERR and loaded tampered cells when HMAC verification failed instead of raising CellCacheError.
bugs.pattern: Cryptographic integrity check logs warning instead of failing closed

bugs.title: soma_core/receipts.py uses non-constant-time string comparisons & purges receipt on consume=False
bugs.description: verify_receipt used standard == string equality and deleted receipt IDs from _receipt_store on invalid check even when consume=False.
bugs.pattern: Timing side channel in token verification and destructive state deletion on read

bugs.title: immune_system/verification/arbiter.py omits import_guard from TOOL_TO_CATEGORY
bugs.description: arbiter.py TOOL_TO_CATEGORY mapping omitted import_guard tool evidence, causing import guard failures to be misclassified as agent convergences.
bugs.pattern: Tool omitted from category dictionary in evidence arbiter

bugs.title: enzymes/post_session_hook.sh shell code injection & \U unicode crash
bugs.description: Unquoted heredoc in enzymes/post_session_hook.sh interpolated git commit logs directly into inline python script, enabling shell/python injection and crashing on git commit messages containing unicode escapes like \U or bash syntax.
bugs.pattern: Unquoted heredoc interpolates unescaped shell variables into inline script

bugs.title: soma_mcp/cell_cache.py fail-closed HMAC & verify_manifest bypass
bugs.description: CellCache._verify_integrity raised CellCacheError on HMAC failure but caller caught and ignored it or loaded empty cache instead of failing closed; get_cells() returned tampered state when manifest verification failed.
bugs.pattern: Cryptographic integrity verification error caught and downgraded to empty or partial state

bugs.title: enzymes/outcome_engine.py telemetry mapping contract drift
bugs.description: outcome_engine.py expected events in signals.jsonl to carry legacy field names while soma_sdk/telemetry.py serialized canonical normalized event schemas, dropping outcome events during replay.
bugs.pattern: Telemetry reader field mapping drifts from canonical telemetry writer schema

bugs.title: enzymes/cell_*.sh infinite root-walk loop on container/Windows drive roots
bugs.description: Upward directory traversal in cell_create.sh, cell_signal.sh, team_sync.sh, and cell_transfer.sh checked [[ "$curr" == "/" ]] but looped infinitely on Windows drive roots (C:) or container boundaries where dirname returned current path.
bugs.pattern: Directory walk loop termination condition assumes POSIX root slash only

bugs.title: install/uninstall.sh orphaned rule bodies in CLAUDE.md
bugs.description: install/uninstall.sh used sed to delete Soma rules from CLAUDE.md by matching start marker but failed to remove trailing rule bodies or truncated to EOF if end marker was missing, corrupting user CLAUDE.md.
bugs.pattern: Multiline section deletion regex truncates past section boundary or orphans content

bugs.title: soma_sdk/governance.py layer inversion import of MCP JIT engine
bugs.description: soma_sdk/governance.py imported parse_frontmatter from soma_mcp.jit_engine, creating an architectural layer inversion where base SDK depended on MCP server implementation and triggered cyclic imports.
bugs.pattern: Base SDK imports higher-layer MCP server implementation module

bugs.title: enzymes/oracle_checkpoint.py bare sibling imports breaking packaged module
bugs.description: oracle_checkpoint.py used bare import ttc_oracle and import cell_fitness which failed when executed as a module or imported outside enzymes/ directory without sys.path injection.
bugs.pattern: Direct sibling script import without package-relative or sys.path resolution

bugs.title: soma_cli/init.py missing kiro platform support
bugs.description: soma init lacked detection, steering directory resolution, and help choices for the kiro agent platform, rejecting initialization on valid kiro environments.
bugs.pattern: Platform enumeration omitted newly supported agent environment

bugs.title: soma_cli/demote.py core rules demotion vulnerability
bugs.description: soma demote permitted users to demote protected core genome rules (such as cost-optimization, providence, and git-workflow) into inactive cells, evading governance safeguards.
bugs.pattern: Destructive mutation command lacks validation guard on protected core rules

bugs.title: enzymes/escalation_sentinel.sh file count vs line count & Rule 6 downgrade
bugs.description: get_diff_size in escalation_sentinel.sh counted changed file lines instead of added/deleted diff lines, under-reporting changeset size, and Rule 6 downgraded prior high-severity escalations back to LOW.
bugs.pattern: Escalation threshold evaluates wrong metric and permits later rules to downgrade severity

bugs.title: enzymes/cell_fitness.py ZeroDivisionError on telomere_days
bugs.description: decayed_fitness calculation crashed with ZeroDivisionError when cell telomere_days was set to 0 or None, blocking fitness evaluations across the entire repository.
bugs.pattern: Division by unvalidated zero or None metadata configuration value

bugs.title: tests/test_inference_provider.py patch('google.genai.Client') ModuleNotFoundError in clean CI
bugs.description: Direct patch('google.genai.Client') in test suite caused ModuleNotFoundError across Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS CI runners where optional google-genai dependency was not pre-installed in the clean environment.
bugs.pattern: Optional third-party dependencies patched directly instead of hermetically mocked via sys.modules

bugs.title: soma_mcp/jit_engine.py unconstrained JIT context token bloat (Issue #75)
bugs.description: Lack of token budget clamping in express() permitted long cell bodies to flood agent context windows, causing output token waste and context degradation.
bugs.pattern: Context injection engine lacks cumulative token estimation and budget enforcement clamps

bugs.title: soma_mcp/jit_engine.py post-generation rejection token waste from unseeded constraints (Issue #77)
bugs.description: Agents generated complete file diffs before inspecting file-specific invariants and anti-pattern traps. Subsequent rejection in proposal evaluation wasted drafting tokens.
bugs.pattern: Downstream validation gates reject changes that could have been prevented with upstream pre-seed context

bugs.title: Host API Key Exfiltration & SSRF via Workspace Config
bugs.description: resolve_key() only excludes keys containing 'API_KEY', allowing OPENAI_BASE_URL to be loaded from an untrusted workspace soma.conf. Soma resolves host OPENAI_API_KEY and forwards it to the attacker-specified endpoint in HTTP Authorization headers during inference.
bugs.pattern: Network base URLs read from untrusted workspace configs without isolating host credential forwarding

bugs.title: Command Safety Shell Interpreter Bypass via Bundled Short Flags
bugs.description: unwrap_command_stage() checks shell flags strictly against ('-c', '/c', '-Command', '-command'). Commands invoked with bundled short flags (e.g. bash -lc, sh -ec) fail to match and evade destructive command inspection.
bugs.pattern: Exact string equality checks on command-line flags fail against POSIX short-flag bundling

bugs.title: Destructive rm -rf Screening Bypass via Trailing Slashes
bugs.description: evaluate_rm() checks targets against RM_DANGEROUS_TARGETS without path normalization or trailing slash stripping. Dangerous targets with trailing slashes (rm -rf ./, rm -rf ../, rm -rf ~/ ) bypass destructive command detection.
bugs.pattern: String matching on filesystem paths fails due to unnormalized trailing slashes

bugs.title: Authentication Bypass in MCP Server tools/call on Omitted Session Token
bugs.description: _sessionToken validation in tools/call is guarded by 'if client_token is not None:'. If a client omits _sessionToken, verification is skipped entirely and active_session_id falls back to _session_token or 'default', granting unauthenticated callers tool execution authority.
bugs.pattern: Authentication check guards skip validation entirely when credentials are absent instead of failing closed

bugs.title: ast.literal_eval Unhandled Exceptions in Function Signature Reconstructor
bugs.description: During AST signature reconstruction for LLM verification prompts, default_val = ast.literal_eval(default_node) crashes on non-literal default expressions (e.g. function calls, path objects, module constants), failing signature extraction.
bugs.pattern: ast.literal_eval called on arbitrary AST expressions without handling ValueError/SyntaxError or falling back to ast.unparse

bugs.title: layer1_by_tool Dictionary Collision Overwrites Multi-Target Evidence in Arbiter
bugs.description: layer1_by_tool = {e.tool: e for e in layer1_evidence} overwrites earlier tool results when multiple target files produce evidence for the same tool. If target A failed and target B passed, only target B is retained, masking failures in adjudication.
bugs.pattern: Dictionary comprehension keys on tool name instead of (tool, target) tuple or list grouping, causing evidence overwrites

bugs.title: Architectural Layer Inversion: soma_core Importing soma_mcp
bugs.description: checkpoint_checks.py in soma_core imports parse_frontmatter from soma_mcp.jit_engine. Layer 0 Core violates architectural boundary by depending upwards on Layer 2 MCP server.
bugs.pattern: Low-level core module imports higher-level porcelain server module, breaking layer decoupling

bugs.title: Missing CLI Output Sanitization & C1 Terminal Escape Injection Gaps
bugs.description: sanitize_display() ignores 8-bit C1 control codes (\u0080-\u009F) and DCS sequences. In addition, soma_cli/verify.py prints out-of-tree filenames directly to stderr without sanitization, permitting terminal control injection via crafted filenames.
bugs.pattern: Terminal display sanitization omits 8-bit control sequences and CLI handlers output raw filenames to stderr

bugs.title: Google GenAI SDK Automatic Function Calling (AFC) Advisory Warning Stderr Pollution
bugs.description: google-genai SDK defaults to enabling Automatic Function Calling (AFC) in Models.generate_content when config is omitted, emitting an advisory warning to stderr advising against direct AFC in generate_content. GeminiProvider must pass config with automatic_function_calling disabled.
bugs.pattern: Upstream SDK defaults trigger advisory warnings on stderr when default configuration options are omitted

bugs.title: Git worktree pre-commit hook installation and detection failure
bugs.description: In git worktrees, .git is a file containing 'gitdir: <path>' rather than a directory. (project_root / '.git' / 'hooks').is_dir() returned False, causing soma init to silently skip pre-commit hook installation and soma doctor to falsely report that hooks were missing.
bugs.pattern: Git hook installation or detection assumes .git is always a directory rather than resolving worktree gitdir pointers

bugs.title: Cell creation omits required enforcement frontmatter field
bugs.description: create_cell() generated cells without the required 'enforcement' frontmatter field, causing newly generated cells (especially vacuoles and walls) to fail soma checkpoint cell_conventions checks during pre-commit.
bugs.pattern: Cell generation utility omits schema fields required by checkpoint conventions validator

bugs.title: Release verification in CI publish workflow falls back to whole-file mutation testing
bugs.description: In GitHub Actions release workflows (publish.yml on release tags), GITHUB_BASE_REF is unset and origin/main points to HEAD. While resolve_target_files correctly fell back to HEAD~1, runner._get_modified_lines did not include HEAD~1 in candidate git diff commands and verify.py did not pass diff_base to run_layer1. Consequently, modified line resolution returned None, causing Layer 1 verification to fall back to legacy whole-file mutation testing and failing CI.
bugs.pattern: CI release workflow lacks base PR reference and verification runner lacks HEAD~1 diff candidate

bugs.title: Unfiltered repository walk in call_graph reads non-source and build artifact binaries
bugs.description: In call_graph.check and check_normalized, external call site searching used os.walk without excluding language build directories (e.g. target/) and without checking file extensions. In projects with large compiled outputs, multi-gigabyte binary files (such as .rlib, object files, and debug symbols) were read into memory as text, causing memory exhaustion and system freeze.
bugs.pattern: Repository walk lacks .gitignore awareness and source extension allowlist filtering

bugs.title: Windows: Rust AST driver slot hard-codes python3, so doctor --fix and the Rust call graph fail on python.org installs
bugs.description: soma_core/ast/detect.py provisions the Rust driver slot as `python3 .soma/drivers/rust_ast.py`. A python.org install on Windows ships python.exe but no python3.exe, so ASTDriverRunner failed with WinError 2, the Rust call graph raised ASTDriverError, and `soma doctor --fix` provisioned the slot and reported it broken in the same run. CI's windows-latest image resolves python3, so CI stayed green. The runner and doctor now resolve a bare python3/python that is not on PATH to sys.executable; slots.yaml keeps the portable name.
bugs.pattern: Interpreter name hard-coded in a generated command instead of resolved at run time

bugs.title: Async storage test never ran on CI, and two symlink tests errored on Windows without symlink privilege
bugs.description: tests/unit/core/test_storage.py::test_async_atomic_write_text is marked @pytest.mark.anyio, but anyio was in neither the [dev] extras nor CI's pinned test dependencies. On CI (pytest 8.3.4) the test was skipped with PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning on every OS, so it never ran; under pytest 9 (an unpinned [dev] install) it failed. Separately, test_somayaml.py and test_workspace_uninitialized.py called symlink_to() directly, so on Windows without Developer Mode or admin rights they raised WinError 1314 instead of skipping. anyio is now a dev and CI dependency, the 'async def functions are not natively supported' warning is an error, and both tests use conftest.symlink_or_skip.
bugs.pattern: Missing test plugin degrades to a silent skip instead of a failure

bugs.title: soma uninstall --platform claude deletes entire CLAUDE.md including user content and leaves MCP config
bugs.description: soma_cli/platforms/claude.py unconditionally unlinked CLAUDE.md upon uninstall, permanently destroying user-authored configuration and custom instructions. Additionally, uninstall left behind soma entries in .mcp.json. Fixed: ClaudeAdapter now delimits Soma sections with SOMA:START/END markers, strips only the Soma-governed block on uninstall, removes the entire file only if no user content remains, and cleans up soma from mcpServers in .mcp.json.
bugs.pattern: Adapter uninstall unlinks shared platform configuration file instead of excising injected section

bugs.title: soma init --platform claude installs rules into <project>/.claude instead of ~/.claude causing doctor and status failures
bugs.description: soma_cli/init.py passed args._project_root as the home override to get_rules_dir(). Because soma_cli/cli.py assigns args._project_root = args.ws.root on every command, soma init treated the workspace as the user home, installing rules to <project>/.claude/ while doctor, status, and uninstall looked in ~/.claude/. Right after init, doctor reported no rules found and status reported 0 active rules. Fixed: soma_cli/init.py now resolves home via _home or _home_override, maintaining path parity with doctor, status, and uninstall.
bugs.pattern: Project root erroneously passed as home directory override during target path resolution

bugs.title: soma status always reports Core rules: 0 active due to cli.py setting _project_root
bugs.description: soma_cli/cli.py assigned args._project_root = args.ws.root for all commands. soma_cli/status.py checked if _project_root is not None to branch into test mode, causing production runs to attempt discovering rules from an uninstalled temporary repo path, resulting in 'Core rules: 0 active'. Fixed: decoupled _project_root workspace resolution from test_mode.
bugs.pattern: Internal test seam flag conflated with general workspace root configuration

bugs.title: soma uninstall --platform claude does not undo soma init
bugs.description: soma uninstall --platform claude only removed CLAUDE.md and cleaned .mcp.json, leaving behind 5 starter rule markdown files in ~/.claude/, workspace .mcp.json, and the git pre-commit hook block installed by soma init. Fixed: uninstall now cleans installed rule files, cleans both target and workspace .mcp.json, and excises the git pre-commit hook block.
bugs.pattern: Asymmetric lifecycle where uninstall cleans only a subset of files written by init

bugs.title: Discrepancy between init and install for Claude rules and missing local flag on init
bugs.description: soma install --platform claude --local wrote a 10-line filename stub instead of full rule text, whereas soma init copied full markdown rule files. Furthermore, soma init lacked a --local flag to target <project>/.claude. Fixed: unified ClaudeAdapter.render_config() to render full rule content across both init and install, and added --local support to soma init.
bugs.pattern: Multiple commands performing similar configuration rendering with inconsistent depth and scopes

bugs.title: soma uninstall --dry-run printed past-tense Uninstalled instead of would uninstall
bugs.description: soma uninstall --dry-run printed 'Uninstalled <file>' using past tense instead of standard dry-run notation '[dry-run] Would uninstall <file>', misleading users into believing deletions occurred. Fixed across all platform adapters.
bugs.pattern: Dry-run mode shares identical logging output strings with destructive execution path

bugs.title: MCP server shutdown reflector invokes make test when make is missing, scoring cells -1.0
bugs.description: When a client disconnected from soma-mcp, the shutdown handler invoked detect_test_runner() which preferred Makefile test targets even if 'make' was not installed on the system (common on Windows). The execution failed with returncode 127, recording tests FAILED and degrading all cell fitness to -1.0. Fixed: detect_test_runner() verifies make availability with shutil.which('make'), and _run_verify treats exit code 127 as unverified/command-not-found rather than test failure.
bugs.pattern: Build tool invoked without verifying binary existence, penalizing system state on missing tools

bugs.title: Mutation tester baseline check obscures root causes of unmutated test failures
bugs.description: When the unmutated baseline test run failed, mutation_tester reported a blanket 'Baseline tests fail against the unmutated code; cannot assess mutations', hiding whether the failure was due to a missing pytest binary, process timeout under load, or actual assertion/import error. Fixed: captured structured TestRunResult and surfaced rich diagnostic details in the baseline failure reason.
bugs.pattern: Generic error message swallows subprocess exit codes and stderr during prerequisite checks

bugs.title: Antigravity drops 5 core rules (META.md, gitflow-review-gate.md, core-change-protocol.md, ci-green-before-release.md, no-pre-existing-excuse.md) due to missing trigger/description frontmatter and META.md installer filter
bugs.description: Five core rules in rules/ declared activation: instead of the Antigravity-required trigger: (always_on / model_decision) and description: fields, and aegis_cli/platforms/base.py explicitly filtered out META.md during installation. Consequently, the IDE dropped all 5 rules from <user_rules>, bypassing mandatory JIT scanning and PR review gates.
bugs.pattern: Platform rule loader silently ignores rule files missing required frontmatter keys or filtered by installer

bugs.title: JIT engine, sentinels, metrics, and lifecycle engines ignore modern rule types (invariant, trap, boundary, persona, contract) and .aegis/rules/ directory
bugs.description: After migrating rules to .aegis/rules/ with modern frontmatter types (invariant, trap, boundary, persona, contract), jit_engine.py still checked type == 'wall', sentinels.py and metrics.py hardcoded .soma/cells, and lifecycle constants only mapped vacuole <-> wall. Fixed: added full support for modern rule types and .aegis/rules/ across JIT, sentinels, metrics, and lifecycle engines.
bugs.pattern: Schema vocabulary migration updates directory names without updating runtime type dispatch tables

bugs.title: aegis migrate moves rule directories to .aegis/rules/ without upgrading YAML frontmatter type fields
bugs.description: aegis_cli/migrate.py moved .soma/cells/{walls,vacuoles,membranes,chloroplasts,plasmodesmata} to .aegis/rules/{invariants,traps,boundaries,personas,contracts} without upgrading the YAML frontmatter type: field inside each migrated markdown file. Fixed: run_migrate now upgrades legacy frontmatter type values to modern rule types.
bugs.pattern: Filesystem migration moves files without transforming embedded schema type identifiers

bugs.title: generate_ci_report crashes with TypeError when changed_files is None and outputs legacy Soma/Cell markdown headers
bugs.description: aegis_core/enforcement.py passed changed_files=None into _format_markdown() when changed_files was omitted, crashing on len(changed_files), and rendered 'Soma CI Outcome Report' / 'Cells matched' instead of Aegis / Rule branding. Fixed: normalized changed_files before formatting and updated markdown report to Aegis / Rule terminology.
bugs.pattern: Optional list parameter resolved locally for matching but passed un-normalized to formatter

bugs.title: Pre-commit hook and init check ignore .aegis/rules and .aegis/enforcement in pure Aegis workspaces
bugs.description: aegis_cli/hooks/runtime.py hardcoded repo_root / '.soma' / 'cells' and '.soma/enforcement' in run_pre_commit(), and aegis_cli/init.py only checked '.soma' in check_existing_install(). Fixed: both modules now prioritize .aegis/rules and .aegis/enforcement with fallback to .soma.
bugs.pattern: Lifecycle hooks hardcode legacy hidden directory path after workspace namespace migration
